About this blog

This is the development blog for Critique Canvas - a community hub built on the Bla+Bla platform for artists who want precise, spatial feedback on their work.

Rather than vague comments floating below an image, Critique Canvas lets community members click directly on a specific area of an uploaded artwork and leave a pinned annotation at that exact location. Feedback becomes spatial, contextual, and genuinely actionable.

What this blog covers

Each post documents a stage of the design and development process — from interpreting the brief and generating ideas, through defining requirements and designing the data model, to making technical decisions and evaluating the final prototype.

The blog is written as part of DECO2017: Advanced Web Design at the University of Sydney, Semester 1 2026.

The stack

Critique Canvas is built on the Bla+Bla prototype template using MojoJS for routes and server-rendered templates, HTMX for partial updates without page reloads, and SQLite for persistent relational data storage.

About the author

Hi, I'm Mehak Arya - a design student at the University of Sydney studying Interaction Design. I care about building things that feel intentional: interfaces that solve real problems for specific communities rather than generic tools dressed up in nice UI.

Outside of uni, I run creative events, make art, and think a lot about how digital spaces can feel more human. Critique Canvas came from a problem I experience personally as an artist - vague feedback that doesn't help you improve - and building it has been the most satisfying project I've worked on so far.

This blog documents my thinking throughout the process. If you're curious about the project or want to connect, find me on LinkedIn.
